# Radios

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use radios when users must choose exactly one option from a small, visible set.

## When to use

- Use for one answer from a small set where seeing every option helps users compare.
- Use inline radios only for short, familiar binary choices such as Yes and No.

## When not to use

- Use checkboxes when more than one answer may be selected.
- Use a select or autocomplete when the option set is too long to scan.
- Do not preselect an answer unless it is a genuine, safe default.

## Anatomy

- **Fieldset and legend (required):** A fieldset groups the question and all radio options.
- **Radio group (required):** A govuk-radios container carries the enhancement hook.
- **Radio items (required):** Native inputs share one name and each has a unique ID, value and associated label.
- **Conditional content:** An option may reveal one small, directly related follow-up region.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stacked | `div` | `govuk-radios` | The default for most radio questions. |
| Inline | `div` | `govuk-radios`, `govuk-radios--inline` | Short binary choices such as Yes and No. |
| Small | `div` | `govuk-radios`, `govuk-radios--small` | A compact expert interface after testing target size and usability. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-radios when using conditional content.
- Without JavaScript, conditional content remains visible and server validation remains authoritative.
- Do not reveal complex questions or another radio group conditionally; use a new page.
- Retain the selected value after validation errors.

## Accessibility contract

- Use native radio inputs inside a fieldset with a visible legend.
- Associate labels, hints, errors and conditional content using unique IDs and official attributes.
- Ensure options remain understandable in source order and with styling removed.

## Content rules

- Write mutually exclusive, non-overlapping options that complete the legend's question.
- Use a divider such as “or” only to separate a distinct final alternative.
- Keep labels concise and add item hints only where necessary.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.error`

## HTML examples

### Yes or no

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group"><fieldset class="govuk-fieldset"><legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend">Have you changed your name?</legend><div class="govuk-radios govuk-radios--inline" data-module="govuk-radios"><div class="govuk-radios__item"><input class="govuk-radios__input" id="changed-name" name="changedName" type="radio" value="yes"><label class="govuk-label govuk-radios__label" for="changed-name">Yes</label></div><div class="govuk-radios__item"><input class="govuk-radios__input" id="changed-name-2" name="changedName" type="radio" value="no"><label class="govuk-label govuk-radios__label" for="changed-name-2">No</label></div></div></fieldset></div>
```
